explication:
## Purpose and entry points
TamaPoke is Arduino firmware for a Pokémon-inspired virtual pet on a Waveshare ESP32-S3 round AMOLED board, plus asset-generation/upload tooling and a browser installer. Firmware entry point and UI/game loop: `TamaPoke.ino`. Browser installation entry: `web/index.html`; asset pipeline begins in `tools/`.

## Firmware orchestration and UI
`TamaPoke.ino` initializes board peripherals, restores state, runs timed game updates, renders all screens, interprets touch gestures, handles serial commands, and coordinates audio. It is the integration boundary between domain logic and hardware/rendering.
- `TamaPoke.ino`
- `pin_config.h`

## Pet domain and persistence
The core state machine owns pet identity, needs, aging/offline catch-up, egg generation, genetics, evolution eligibility, endings, Pokédex registration, streak/bond, medals, and training. State is persisted in ESP32 NVS; the Pokédex number is the pet identity. UI invokes this layer for care actions and lifecycle decisions.
- `pet.h`
- `pet.cpp`
- `dex.h`

## Species and localization data
Generated static headers keep firmware runtime-independent from external APIs. `dex.h` contains the 151-species table, evolution/rarity/type information, and localized name access; `species.h` provides fallback/UI sprite data. UI strings are separate seven-language tables.
- `dex.h`
- `species.h`
- `i18n.cpp`

## Sprite storage, animation, and USB transfer
The runtime loads primary PMD/TPK2 animated sprites and thumbnail data from microSD into PSRAM, with legacy/fallback formats retained. It also exposes the serial PUT/LS transfer protocol used to populate SD without removing it. This is the boundary between the firmware and the large, versioned sprite corpus.
- `sdmon.h`
- `sdmon.cpp`
- `tools/sdcard/mons/thumbs.bin`

## Hardware services
Dedicated adapters manage RTC/PMU and audio. RTC time enables offline progression and time-of-day backgrounds; AXP2101 supplies battery, brightness, and power-button handling. ES8311 audio is driven through ESP32 I2S with non-blocking tone synthesis.
- `rtcbat.cpp`
- `audio.cpp`
- `pin_config.h`

## Offline build and asset pipeline
Python tools generate firmware data and transform PMD SpriteCollab assets into SD-ready sprite binaries and thumbnail packs. Data generation flows from curated species/stats/name sources to generated headers; asset packing flows to `tools/sdcard/mons/`, then either serial upload or the web bundle.
- `tools/dex_data.py`
- `tools/gen_dex.py`
- `tools/pack_pmd.py`

## Distribution and external dependencies
The target runtime is ESP32 Arduino on an ESP32-S3 with OPI PSRAM, FAT-capable flash partition, microSD, CO5300 QSPI display, CST9217 I2C touch, PCF85063 RTC, AXP2101 PMU, and ES8311/I2S audio. Arduino libraries include Arduino_GFX, SensorLib, XPowersLib, U8g2 font data, and ESP_I2S. PMD SpriteCollab supplies sprite source material; PokéAPI informs base stats/names during generation. The HTTPS-hosted installer flashes `web/firmware/tamapoke.bin` via ESP Web Tools and transfers `web/sprites.pak` via Web Serial.
- `web/index.html`
- `web/firmware/tamapoke.bin`
- `web/sprites.pak`
